schedule.rationale: At Risk. 315 points remain at about 28 per sprint, roughly 11 sprints or 22 weeks of delivery, and the test environment is still missing (S3, S5). The current date is not stated, so the margin before 1 March 2027 cannot be confirmed, but it looks too thin.

scope.rationale: At Risk. Scope grew 47%, from 310 to 455 points, through 19 unpriced stories that bypassed change control (S1). The fixed price and fixed go-live did not change (S2).

quality.rationale: Problematic. The scenario gives no defect, test coverage or review data, so quality cannot be confirmed as sound. Integration testing is blocked until the treasury test environment exists (S5).

risk_control.rationale: At Risk. Change control was bypassed, no risk response is recorded, and the penalty exposure of 4,000 euros per working day is not managed (S1, S2).

stakeholder_confidence.rationale: At Risk. The client director was told last week that delivery is on track, which the facts do not support (S7). Correcting this will be harder the longer it waits.

risks.description: Remaining 315 points cannot be delivered by 1 March 2027 at the current pace of about 28 points per sprint, so the regulatory go-live is missed and penalties accrue.
risks.mitigation: Re-baseline the scope to a regulatory core that fits the remaining capacity, agree the cut with the client in writing, and set a fixed go-live scope list before the 3 December steering committee.

risks.description: Further unpriced scope additions continue through sprint reviews, widening the gap between the fixed price and the real cost of delivery.
risks.mitigation: Stop accepting new stories in sprint reviews. Route every request through a written change request with an estimate and price, and get client approval before it enters a sprint.

risks.description: The treasury integration stays blocked because the client-promised test environment for September does not exist, so payment integration cannot be tested before go-live.
risks.mitigation: Ask the client for a committed date for the environment in writing. Meanwhile, build a mock of the treasury interface so development and testing can continue, and decide whether payment is in the 1 March scope.

risks.description: The client director holds an optimistic view of delivery, so a later correction could damage trust and make the decisions needed harder to get.
risks.mitigation: Send the client director a factual status that shows remaining points, velocity, the blocked integration and the go-live risk, and agree a fortnightly reporting rhythm.

risks.description: Two developers are working over 50 hours a week, which risks burnout, resignation and further slowdown of delivery.
risks.mitigation: Set a weekly hours limit, rebalance the work across the team of seven, and remove blockers that force extra hours. Track weekly hours and review them with the project manager.

stabilize.goal: Stop the scope and status situation getting worse and make the real position visible to the client.

actions.description: Freeze scope: no new story enters a sprint without a signed change request.
actions.success_signal: Sprint backlog at the end of sprint 2 contains no story that lacks an approved change request.

actions.description: Cut overtime for the two developers working over 50 hours a week by moving work to other team members.
actions.success_signal: Both developers log under 45 hours a week for two consecutive weeks.

actions.description: Send the client director a factual status showing 315 remaining points, current velocity and the blocked treasury integration.
actions.success_signal: Written status is accepted by the client director and a review date is agreed.

actions.description: Obtain a written commitment from the client on the date for the treasury test environment.
actions.success_signal: A dated commitment for the test environment is recorded in the project log.

recover.goal: Agree a re-baselined scope and deliverable plan that fits the remaining capacity before 1 March 2027.

actions.description: Price the 19 added stories through a change request and agree which of them stay in the 1 March release.
actions.success_signal: Signed change request covering all 19 stories, with each one marked in scope for 1 March or deferred.

actions.description: Agree the 1 March scope list with the client, deferring payment integration and mobile document upload if they are not essential for go-live.
actions.success_signal: Written scope list for 1 March whose total points fit the remaining sprints at the measured velocity.

actions.description: Build a mock of the treasury interface so the rest of the payment flow can be developed and tested.
actions.success_signal: Payment flow runs end to end against the mock in the test environment by the end of sprint 4.

sustain.goal: Keep the project on the agreed plan and stop the same problems from coming back.

actions.description: Keep change control in force so that every new story is logged, estimated, priced and approved.
actions.success_signal: Sprint 6 review shows zero stories added without an approved change request.

actions.description: Report measured velocity and remaining points at every sprint review and compare them with the plan.
actions.success_signal: Each sprint review shows velocity and remaining points, with variance from plan under 10 percent.

actions.description: Run a go/no-go readiness check for the regulatory cutover on 1 March 2027.
actions.success_signal: Readiness checklist for 1 March is complete and signed off at the end of sprint 6.

stakeholder_updates.executive: The project will not deliver the full current scope by 1 March 2027 at the present pace. At the 3 December steering committee we need a decision to re-baseline scope with the client, including a priced change request for the 19 added stories and an agreed core scope for go-live. Without that decision, the penalty of 4,000 euros per working day continues to accrue and the regulatory deadline is at risk.
stakeholder_updates.delivery_team: Scope will be frozen, so new requests are no longer added to sprints without a change request. Two developers will move back below 45 hours a week, and work will be rebalanced across the team. Your priority is the 1 March core scope, and we will confirm the list in writing. The treasury integration will be built against a mock until the client test environment is ready.
stakeholder_updates.customer: We want to be open about where the project stands. The scope grew during the build, and this has pushed the work beyond what can be delivered by 1 March 2027 at the current pace. We are proposing to agree a core release for the regulatory deadline, with the remaining features scheduled afterwards, and we will confirm the details with you in writing. We also need a firm date for the test environment needed for the treasury integration.

decision_memo.context: The project has 315 points remaining against a fixed go-live of 1 March 2027, with a penalty of 4,000 euros per working day of delay. The current velocity cannot deliver the full scope in time. The decision must be made at the 3 December steering committee so that the client can agree the change before the sprints needed for go-live are committed.

options.title: Keep the full scope and the fixed date, and continue with current capacity
options.trade_offs: Keeps everything the client has asked for, but the team cannot deliver 315 points at 28 points per sprint by 1 March. It means continued overtime, certain penalties and a larger gap between the fixed price and actual cost.

options.title: Re-baseline with the client: agree a priced change request and a core scope for 1 March, deferring the rest
options.trade_offs: Protects the regulatory deadline and the fixed price with a clear scope cut, but the client may refuse to pay for or defer features. It needs a formal change request and an honest status conversation with the client director.

options.title: Add people to the team to increase delivery speed
options.trade_offs: Could raise capacity, but new people need onboarding and will slow the current team in the short term. The fixed price is already 62 percent spent, so added cost would fall on the supplier unless the client agrees to pay for it.

decision_memo.recommendation: Choose option 2. Agree a priced change request and a core scope for 1 March 2027, with the remaining stories scheduled after go-live. This is the only option that protects the regulatory deadline without relying on sustained overtime or unfunded hiring. It must be taken to the client before the 3 December steering committee so that the committee can confirm it.
success_metrics: Signed change request covering the 19 added stories before 3 December
Agreed 1 March scope list whose points fit the remaining sprints at measured velocity
Zero stories added to sprints without an approved change request from the decision date onwards
Both overworked developers below 45 hours a week for two consecutive weeks
Written date for the treasury test environment confirmed by the client
